observed_warning.upgrade_effect: Existing Gradle 9.8.1 log says this cross-build undeclared consumption becomes an error in Gradle 10.

separate_warning_out_of_scope.description: Configuration.setVisible(boolean) deprecation, scheduled for Gradle 11; output-target exclusions do not claim to resolve this.

observed_warning.limits: Diagnostics identify producer tasks and the repository-root location, not a concrete formatted Kotlin file. Current producer output directories contain no .kt/.kts. Do not describe class/property outputs as having been formatted.

official_documentation.use: Documents target and targetExclude configuration. Exact installed-version defaults were checked against gradle/8.10.2 source, not inferred from current README alone.

official_documentation.version: current documentation displayed 9.8.2; local wrapper is 9.8.1
official_documentation.use: Explains accidental producer/consumer dependency and execution-order sensitivity; real consumers need provider/task dependencies. This formatter should instead exclude unintended outputs. Exact 9.8.1 web page could not be opened by browsing tool; observed warning text is preserved from the actual 9.8.1 build.
File trees use a base directory and Ant-style include/exclude patterns; explicit exclusions constrain source scope.

spotless_defaults.excluded: Root .git/.gradle, root buildDirectory, and normal getSubprojects() buildDirectory values are excluded automatically. Included builds are not visited by getSubprojects().
spotless_defaults.consequence: The eight observed app/build KSP/backups .kt files match the raw glob but are already excluded by Spotless defaults. The included build convention/build subtree is not automatically excluded.

target_exclude_implementation.behavior: target.minus(targetExclude) is the task target. Gradle 9.8.1 SubtractingFileCollection.java:56-59 enumerates left files and removes right files. This supports the documented targetExclude API as the least invasive candidate; its actual warning-removal effect still needs a Gradle check.

source_findings.classification: Generated included-build directories are in the broad source tree scope structurally. No currently existing generated .kt/.kts under build-logic/convention/build was observed; the warning alone proves cross-build output overlap, not generated Kotlin formatting.

static_inventory.method: Read-only rg --files -uu for *.kt/*.kts plus git ls-files; model automatic exclusions from exact Spotless version source. Not an executed Gradle input-file listing.

recommendation.classification: H build tooling / formatting scope; independent of theme behavior patch.

minimum_candidate.placement: Inside existing spotless.kotlin block, after target(...)
minimum_candidate.why: Excludes only the actual included-build output subtree shared by all three reported producers, preserving existing target strings and their automatic normal-subproject exclusions. Retains root scripts, all app/codegen Kotlin, and all 12 authored build-logic Kotlin/scripts.

optional_broader_policy.tradeoff: Covers future nested included-build outputs and cache directories without enumerating projects; no current tracked Kotlin is removed. Broader than the observed issue and may omit future authored paths with a literal build directory segment. Not required for the minimum observed fix.

recommendation.if_actual_warning_persists: Inspect executed task input structure before expanding the patch. A direct fileTree(projectDir) target with PatternSet exclusions is a possible fallback, but passing a FileCollection bypasses Spotless string-target automatic exclusions; explicitly preserve root/app/codegen output and .git/.gradle exclusions. Do not switch prematurely.
avoid: Do not exclude the whole build-logic directory or narrow formatting to root src/**: these omit authored convention plugin and build script coverage.
Do not add dependsOn/mustRunAfter to compiler/resource tasks merely to silence a formatter consuming unintended output.
Do not claim generated Kotlin was formatted, all Gradle warnings were fixed, or the candidate is verified without running it.

suggested_followup_validation_not_execut: Use a clean isolated source worktree with existing/warm included-build output directories. Apply only the candidate exclude and run the existing Spotless check with --warning-mode all, ensuring :spotlessKotlin actually executes. A check after deleting all generated directories alone is insufficient to prove the warning is fixed.
Verify the three included-build implicit-dependency warnings disappear while recording unrelated remaining warnings separately. Keep the same wrapper/Spotless versions for the comparison.

Confirm root build.gradle.kts/settings.gradle.kts, normal app/codegen source, and all 12 authored build-logic .kt/.kts remain in scope. Static inventory already proves no current tracked Kotlin path is excluded by the precise candidate.

If extra scope evidence is needed, use disposable sentinels only in that isolated worktree: a generated .kt inside convention/build must be ignored, while a malformed authored convention/src/main/kotlin file must still be detected. Restore sentinels before committing. No new production abstraction or mirror test is needed for this configuration change.
